newsitem.title: USA: Most U.S. spot resids steady to up on weather.
newsitem.headline: Most U.S. spot resids steady to up on weather.

text.p: U.S. spot fuel oil prices mostly were steady to slightly higher again Friday in moderate activity, with recently-hot East Coast weather and forecasts for more heat next week still underpinning the complex.

"The heat this week probably trimmed inventories slightly but it's not enough yet to force utilities back into the market. We're seeing a little utility interest, but there's no panic," said one cash trader.
In New York Harbor, physical one percent inched up slightly to $16.25-50 a barrel, with July one percent paper recovering 20 cents to $16.35-60 with firmer crude.
NYH 0.3 percent high pour held relatively steady at $17.75-18.00, with a July 5 seller seen at $18.25 (delivered).
A trader said a fairly prompt 0.43 percent piece sold at $18.25 (delivered Connecticut). A New England utility was reported looking for 225,000 barrels of 0.7 percent for second-half July delivery.
High sulphurs in New York were flat to up slightly, with three percent now quoted at $14.25-50.
At the U.S. Gulf, three percent notionally held steady at $13.25-50, while one percent slipped more than a quarter to $15.25-50.
Traders said 45,000 barrels of USG 3.5 percent (10 gravity, 250 viscosity) sold at $13. A Florida utility reportedly may soon be looking for some one percent.

New York city gate weekend gas prices slipped more than a nickel Friday to the mid-to-high $2.40s/mmBtu, or $15.56 a barrel equivalent, with July quoted in the mid-$2.40s, or $15.44. Weekend gas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, was talked in the $2.19/mmBtu area, or $13.80, while July gas at the Hub was pegged at $2.17, or $13.67.
